patient_overview.name: Odell Rippin
patient_overview.description: Odell Rippin is an 84-year-old divorced man from Hopatcong, New Jersey, still working full-time, who comes in for a hyperlipidemia and prediabetes follow-up. He is anxious and apologetic, bracing for a scolding before the student even sits down, and he tends to answer questions with long, winding stories about his job, his late wife, or something he read online before circling back to the point. He has read extensively about cholesterol and blood sugar and can quote numbers, but his actual eating is dictated by odd work hours, vending machines, and whatever drive-through is open when his shift ends. He knows something has to change but is torn about where to start, and he has almost no one checking in on him day to day.

demographics.occupation: Toll plaza supervisor / overnight facilities coordinator for a regional transit authority, still working full-time at 84
demographics.cultural_context: Odell grew up in a working-class New Jersey family where his father worked the railroads and meals were whatever could be made quickly between shifts; that pattern of eating around a job rather than around a clock has followed him his whole life. He was raised to see needing help as a weakness, which shapes how reluctant he is now to admit he struggles alone. He values being useful and employed, and takes pride in never having "called out sick in thirty years," even if it means skipping meals or eating from a machine.

medications.name: Simvastatin 10 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: irregular - he often skips it or takes it at a different time, and sometimes doubles up the next day if he forgets, which he does not mention unless asked carefully
medications.patient_concerns: He read online that statins can cause muscle pain and liver problems, so when his legs ache after a long shift standing at the toll plaza, he quietly skips the dose 'just to be safe' without telling anyone.

medications.name: Vitamin B12 5 MG/ML Injectable Solution
medications.frequency: administered periodically as an injectable, per care plan rather than a daily pill
medications.adherence: attends scheduled administration but is vague about exact timing between doses
medications.patient_concerns: He isn't entirely sure why he needs it, assumes it's 'for his blood,' and feels embarrassed asking the nurse to explain again.
